channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: East Kazakhstan Archives Offer Online Services for Documents
item.description: Residents of East Kazakhstan can now access archival services, including certificates and document copies, remotely via the e-government portal. This service is free and helps confirm labor, social, and property rights, as well as pension and inheritance matters.

item.title: Kazakhstan Harvests 18.6 Million Tons of Grain Amid Ongoing Campaign
item.description: Kazakhstan has harvested 18.6 million tons of grain, with 81.5% of the total grain and pulse crop area completed. The average yield is 14.6 centners per hectare. The total sown area reached 24.2 million hectares, an increase of 600,000 hectares from last year.

item.title: Man detained in Almaty for applying drug advertisements on fence
item.description: Police in Almaty detained a man while he was applying drug advertisements to a city fence. According to the Police Department, he received the task via Telegram and was promised money for its completion. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: Four bloggers arrested in Shymkent for using profanity on TikTok
item.description: Four bloggers in Shymkent have been brought to administrative responsibility for violating public order during a TikTok live broadcast. The city's police department reported that the bloggers used indecent language. They were sentenced to administrative detention ranging from 5 to 17 days.

item.title: Three Children Die in Residential Fire in Zhetysu Region; Emergency Services Silent
item.description: Three young children, aged 1, 6, and 8, perished in a house fire in the village of Baktybay, Zhetysu region, on September 25. The fire, which occurred in a four-apartment building, engulfed one apartment. Emergency services have not reported the tragedy.

item.title: China and US Reach Eight-Point Consensus Following Xi Jinping's Visit
item.description: China and the United States have agreed on an eight-point consensus after Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit. Key points include building constructive strategic stability, mutual tariff reduction of approximately $30 billion, and initiating dialogue on AI. The US welcomed the loan of giant pandas.

item.title: Prosecutor General assumes control of investigation into alleged sexual assault at kindergarten
item.description: Uzbekistan's Prosecutor General Nigmatilla Yuldashev has personally taken control of the investigation into an alleged sexual assault at a kindergarten in Uchqo‘rg‘on district, Namangan region. A criminal case has been initiated under articles related to rape and threatening with murder or violence. One suspect has been detained.

item.title: Burnley Coach Expects Dastan Satpayev's Return After International Break
item.description: Burnley manager Vincent Kompany stated that Kazakhstani forward Dastan Satpayev is nearing a return from injury. Satpayev is expected to rejoin the squad for the Championship match against Watford on October 10th, following the international break. His return is seen as a significant boost for the team's tactics.

item.title: Pakistan PM Alleges Afghanistan Used for Attacks Against Pakistan at UN
item.description: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif told the UN General Assembly that armed groups, including TTP and BLA, operate from Afghanistan and conduct attacks targeting Pakistan. He urged Taliban authorities to take decisive action to prevent Afghan territory from being used for such purposes. The Taliban have denied these accusations.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Establishes Commission to Audit Ministry of Defense
item.description: Kazakhstan's President has created a commission to conduct a comprehensive audit of the Ministry of Defense. The commission, led by Aida Balayeva, will also examine financial and logistical support for military units. A report is due within seven days.

item.title: Kazakhstan's disinformation center monitors social media use of Caspian tragedy
item.description: Kazakhstan's Center for Combating Disinformation reports attempts to exploit a Caspian Sea tragedy for social media engagement. The center is tracking unverified information, including AI-generated videos and manipulated footage, being spread online. Some coordinated disinformation campaigns appear to originate from outside Kazakhstan.

item.title: Mural commemorating soldiers lost at sea appears in Almaty
item.description: A mural honoring 14 servicemen who died during exercises in the Caspian Sea on September 24 has appeared on a building in Almaty. The artwork depicts birds flying over the sea with the inscription 'Unforgettable' and the date. A criminal case has been opened.

item.title: Fundraising for Caspian Incident Victims Concludes
item.description: Fundraising for a special fund established to assist families of the deceased and injured military personnel in the Caspian incident has officially concluded. The commission chairman stated that sufficient funds have been collected through the support of various citizens and organizations. Funds will be distributed equitably.

item.title: Funds collected for families of deceased military personnel in Mangystau
item.description: The collection of funds for the families of deceased and injured military personnel in Kazakhstan has officially concluded. The funds will be distributed fairly among the families, according to Bekmurat Zhusipov, head of the special commission.

item.title: Defense Ministry Names Third Surviving Serviceman from Caspian Incident
item.description: Kazakhstan's Defense Ministry has identified Nikita Udlov as the third military serviceman to survive an incident during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea. Udlov, from West Kazakhstan region, joins previously named survivors Beket Myrzagaliyev and Akzhol Temiraliev. Friends expressed relief and support for Udlov's recovery.

item.title: Blast in Pakistan's Dera Ismail Khan Kills 11, Injures 30
item.description: Eleven people were killed and 30 injured in a blast in Dera Ismail Khan, northwestern Pakistan, on Saturday. The Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan claimed responsibility for the attack, which occurred near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area. Rescue teams provided medical assistance to the wounded.

item.title: Kyrgyz Foreign Minister discusses EU sanctions policy with Kaja Kallas
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev met with EU High Representative Kaja Kallas at the UN General Assembly. They discussed bilateral cooperation, joint investment projects in transport, energy, green economy, and digitalization. Kulubaev briefed Kallas on Kyrgyzstan's efforts to prevent sanctions circumvention.

item.title: Tajikistan Studies Uzbekistan's Social Protection Digitization Experience
item.description: Specialists from Tajikistan's Ministry of Health and Social Protection underwent training in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. They studied Uzbekistan's experience in digitizing its social protection system and its national disability assessment model. The delegation also visited local social service centers and a family polyclinic.

item.title: Kazakhstan Officially Concludes Fundraising for Families of Caspian Sea Servicemen
item.description: Fundraising for families of servicemen killed during Caspian Sea exercises has officially concluded, announced Bekmurat Zhusupov, a member of the People's Council of Kazakhstan. A special fund was created to accumulate donations, and the collected funds are deemed sufficient. Distribution to affected families will begin soon.

item.title: Families of Caspian Military Accident Victims to Receive Funds Soon
item.description: Families of military personnel killed and injured during Caspian Sea exercises will soon receive funds from a special foundation. The necessary amount has been collected, and the collection is officially closed. The distribution will be fair and equal, overseen by state and law enforcement officials.

item.title: Almaty's CHP-2 to continue burning coal until the 2030s despite gas conversion
item.description: Almaty's Thermal Power Plant-2 (CHP-2) will continue to burn coal until the 2030s, even after its conversion to gas. Existing coal-fired boilers and turbines will remain operational during peak autumn-winter periods until 2030 and beyond, to ensure uninterrupted energy supply.

item.title: Blogger Sirojiddin Odilov Faces Criminal Charges, Prosecution Seeks Six-Year Sentence
item.description: Blogger Sirojiddin Odilov, known as "Sirojiddin Media," is on trial in the Mirza-Chul District Court for Criminal Cases. The prosecution has requested a six-year prison sentence for the accused, stating the charges are more accurately described as 'slander'.

item.title: Ghormach Health Centre in Badghis Receives $111,000 in Medical Equipment
item.description: The Ghormach district health centre in Badghis province has received 46 medical equipment items worth $111,000, funded by UNHCR. The Taliban Ministry of Public Health stated that another shipment is expected soon. Residents face challenges accessing healthcare services.

item.title: Badakhshan Health System Faces Collapse Amid Abuse and Corruption Allegations
item.description: Residents of Badakhshan express concern over the deteriorating health services provided by the Sanayee Development Organization (SDO). Allegations include misuse of resources, sexual exploitation of health workers by the organization's director, and ties with the Taliban. The SDO's failure to address responsibilities and lack of accountability are major concerns.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Orders Comprehensive Audit of Defense Ministry
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered a comprehensive review of Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense. The commission is tasked with examining financial and logistical aspects of military units and must report initial findings to the president within seven days.

item.title: Explosion in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan kills at least 11, injures 20
item.description: An explosion at a police checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan, killed at least 11 people and injured 20. The victims included men, women, and a child. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Zhezkazgan-Kyzylorda Road to Open in Coming Months
item.description: The modernization of the Zhezkazgan-Kyzylorda highway is 90% complete and expected to open for traffic in the coming months, according to Ulytau region governor Eset Baiken. Work on the Zhezkazgan-Karaganda section will finish this year, and the Ulytau-Arkalyk road repair will conclude in October.

item.title: Former Kazakh Navy Commander: Caspian Sea Exercises Should Have Been Postponed
item.description: Former Commander of the Kazakh Navy, Vice-Admiral Zhandarbek Zhanzakov, believes military leaders are responsible for the deaths of 14 servicemen during Caspian Sea exercises. He stated the exercises should have been postponed or canceled due to worsening weather conditions.

item.title: Children's Ombudsman Demands Action After Kindergarten Sexual Assault in Namangan
item.description: Uzbekistan's Children's Ombudsman has submitted a request to the Ministry of Preschool and School Education regarding a sexual assault case in a Namangan kindergarten. The ombudsman demands strengthened child safety measures, staff background checks, and revised internal control mechanisms in all kindergartens.

item.title: Kazakh Police Contact Users Criticizing Caspian Incident Online
item.description: Several Kazakh social media users reported being contacted by police after posting critical comments about a recent Caspian Sea incident. One user shared an audio recording of a police officer requesting the removal of a post deemed 'against the people' and aimed at preventing protests.

item.title: Uzbekistan Delegation Attends International Training on Medical Devices in Beijing
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan participated in the 5th GHWP (China) Academy international training in Beijing, focusing on advanced medical devices for global public health. The event covered medical device regulation, international harmonization, and innovative medical technologies, offering opportunities to study international experience.

item.title: Business Development Bank Holds Dialogue with Entrepreneurs in Andijan Region
item.description: The Business Development Bank held a dialogue with entrepreneurs in the Andijan region, focusing on supporting business growth, effective investment, and improving banking services. The bank aims to be a financial partner for businesses, assisting with expansion, new projects, equipment acquisition, job creation, and export market entry.

item.title: Graffiti Appears in Almaty Commemorating Soldiers Lost in Caspian Sea Incident
item.description: A graffiti artwork has appeared in Almaty to commemorate 14 soldiers who died during a military exercise in the Caspian Sea on September 24. The artwork depicts the sea, a setting sun, and 14 birds, with the inscription "24.09 Unforgettable. Aktau." Five military officials were detained following the incident.

item.title: Kazakh President Orders Comprehensive Audit of the Ministry of Defense
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree to conduct a comprehensive inspection of the Ministry of Defense. A commission has been formed to oversee this audit, comprising high-ranking officials from the Security Council, Supreme Audit Chamber, Presidential Administration, and other key government bodies.

item.title: Tokayev Establishes Commission for Comprehensive Audit of Defense Ministry
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has formed a commission tasked with conducting a comprehensive audit of the Ministry of Defense. This directive indicates a significant review of the ministry's operations and management.

item.title: Kazakh President Orders Comprehensive Audit of Ministry of Defense
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered the creation of a commission to conduct a comprehensive audit of the Ministry of Defense's affairs. The audit will examine financial and logistical support for military units, with specific officials appointed to lead the commission.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Energy Regulator's Authority to Natural and Liquefied Gas Markets
item.description: Uzbekistan's energy regulator will have expanded powers over natural and liquefied gas markets, according to a presidential decree. The agency will be responsible for developing market principles and regulation in these sectors, previously focusing mainly on electricity. It will also oversee licensing and tariff approvals from 2028.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Foreign Minister Discusses Sanctions Policy with EU's Top Diplomat
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev met with the EU's High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, Josep Borrell, during the UN General Assembly. They discussed bilateral cooperation, investment projects, and Kyrgyzstan's efforts to prevent sanctions circumvention. Both sides agreed to continue dialogue on sanctions.

item.title: Afghan Freedom Front Reports Clashes with Taliban in Nuristan
item.description: The Afghan Freedom Front claims clashes with Taliban forces began Saturday morning in Kamdish district, Nuristan province, and are ongoing. The group alleges the Taliban attacked its positions with ground forces and drones. The Freedom Front stated its forces defended and launched a counter-attack, capturing several Taliban outposts and pushing them back from certain areas.

item.title: Children's Ombudsman Submits Proposal to Ministry Over Kindergarten Abuse Case
item.description: The Children's Ombudsman has submitted a proposal to the Ministry of Preschool and School Education regarding a sexual abuse case involving a child at a kindergarten. The proposal calls for a critical review of the ongoing investigation, addressing identified shortcomings, and holding responsible employees accountable. It also emphasizes strengthening child safety measures across all preschool institutions.
